$comment: What a client keeps out of a metadata update. Read by tests/shared/metadata.test.ts and the Android SharedCorpusTest. A value is a string a stranger chose, and what a server advertises as its limit is what it will accept rather than what it will refuse to forward — nothing checked on the way in, so a display name drawn beside every line could be a megabyte. Keys we never render were kept too, in a map that grows with whatever a server sends.
$cases: `key` and `value` as they arrived. `keep` is null where the update is ignored entirely; otherwise it is what is stored.

cases.name: and trimmed, because a server may pad it
an empty value is a key being cleared, which is worth keeping
a key we never draw is ignored
and so is one that only looks close
a value at the ceiling is kept whole
and something absurd is cut to the same place
